executionPlan: Root-caused F1 (Hips stripped, so the crouch lost its pelvis drop). Baked a Hips height into land.glb and fall.glb in strip-clips. Added a runtime one-sided foot floor in the animator. Added a camera obstacle query (Rapier sphere cast) for F6. Wrote stance and drop tests and proved them red on the old clips. Verified in headless Chrome with a page-side sampler (software GL, so about 8 fps).
summary: F1: land.glb now keeps the Hips rotation and a Hips translation (x and z are the source pelvis travel, y is derived per frame so the lowest foot joint stands on the ground). The trailing foot of the one-knee landing is lowered with a leg IK, and fall.glb gets a planted vertical Hips track. In the browser both feet stay at 0.022 to 0.032 m for the whole land state after 1.6 m and 4 m drops. F6: the follow camera now pulls in through a real sphere-cast query, with 0 frames inside any block in tests and in the browser. Lint, 145 tests and the build in a copy are green. No commit.

criteria.criterion: QA F1 is fixed: during the whole land state after a drop of 1.6 m and of 4 m, both feet stay within 0.05 m of the ground (toe and foot bones measured in the browser against the grounded capsule), the hips visibly crouch, and the blend from fall into land and from land into idle or walk shows no pop; the mechanism (for example a vertical hips offset derived from the source clip applied in game code, or a different source) is explained with evidence.
criteria.evidence: Cause: strip-clips dropped the Hips tracks, so the pelvis stayed at 0.984 m while the folded legs put the feet 0.84 to 0.95 m up. Mechanism: land.glb now carries Hips rotation plus translation (frames 2 to 58 of the source). The Hips y is derived per frame so the avatar's lowest foot or toe joint stands at the rest-stance height, and it matches the source pelvis height within 0.031 m. The trailing foot of the one-knee landing hung up to 0.13 m, so a two-bone leg IK lowers it (largest drop 0.092 m on 35 of 57 frames). fall.glb gets a planted vertical Hips track so a touchdown starts on the ground. At runtime a one-sided foot floor lifts the Hips only while a fall or land action still has weight, so blends never sink the feet. Browser, 4 m end drop: lowest foot 0.022 on all 20 land rows, per-foot max in the land state 0.027 (left) and 0.032 (right), hips world y 0.47 to 0.61 (crouch from 0.98). Browser, 1.6 m side drop (left the ramp side at feet y 1.62): lowest 0.022 on all rows, per-foot 0.022 to 0.032 while the state is land. Caveats: the 4 m run, 4 m walk and 1.6 m walk runs all show a per-foot peak of 0.051 to 0.059 m on the final 2 or 3 rows (labelled idle+land, the 0.25 s blend out of land as the avatar stands up), above 0.05 for about 0.1 s while the state is already idle. No-pop numbers from the unit-level animator sim at 60 Hz: land entry steps 0.07 m per frame or less, with the fall to land fade lengthened from 0.1 to 0.15 s; the blend out never sinks below ground. In the browser the first land row is at 0.021 to 0.022 because fall is planted. A 1.6 m side drop in run mode fell into the void in one attempt (a steering bug in my script) and was re-run without that bug as the walk case; the 4 m run case passed. Screenshots hardland-*-end-*.png.

criteria.criterion: Every clip that changes stance (idle, walk, run, jump, fall, land) is covered by an automated test that evaluates the clip on the avatar skeleton (or a faithful fixture) and asserts the lowest foot height relative to the ground at grounded frames stays within a stated tolerance, and the test fails on the current land clip setup before the fix (red) and passes after (green).
criteria.evidence: components/game/__tests__/stance.test.ts builds the real avatar bone tree from public/avatar.glb (scripts/lib/avatar-rig.mjs reads only the JSON chunk). It evaluates each shipped clip through toGameClip and a mixer and measures the foot and toe joint heights. Tolerance is 0.05 m of ground. idle: every frame within 0.05. walk: a foot reaches the ground and the max lowest foot is 0.12 (no pelvis bob modelled). run: reaches the ground, flight phase under 0.25. jump: push-off start under 0.25, tuck under 0.6, never below ground. fall: every frame within 0.05 (planted). land: every played frame within 0.05, each foot separately, the whole clip within 0.06, bone lengths preserved and the leg never past straight, crouch depth at least 0.3 m. Animator-level sims cover fall to land to idle or walk, soft landing, jump to fall and walk to fall. Red: with the pre-fix land.glb and fall.glb swapped in, 6 of 16 tests fail (output saved in the game-r2 scratch directory as red-run.txt). Green: all 16 pass. Honest limit: walk and run do not meet 0.05 at every frame (0.103 and 0.224 maxima, unchanged approved clips), so their stated tolerances are looser and documented.

criteria.criterion: QA F6 is fixed: walking off the end of the 30 degree ramp (4 m drop) and off its side, the camera never ends inside or behind a level block for any frame (camera position checked against every collider each frame in the browser, plus screenshots of the drop), using the existing obstacle query with a probe that does not get stuck, and followCamera tests cover the drop case.
criteria.evidence: The follow camera previously ignored its ObstacleQuery (void query). It now casts from the pivot to the wanted position with the new cameraProbe.ts (a Rapier ball cast, probe radius 0.2, camera-blocker group, stopAtPenetration false so a probe that starts inside geometry exits instead of sticking at distance 0). It pulls in at once and eases back out with restoreK. followCamera.test.ts (22 tests): the fake query cases, 16 real-Rapier drops (end and side, walk and run, 4 camera yaws) checking every block on every 60 Hz frame (0 frames inside, clearance at least 0.1), red-without-query tests (inside ramp-30 for more than 10 frames at the end drop, and for yaw 2 rad at the side drop), and a not-stuck test (camera back at full distance after walking clear). Browser (page-side check against all 11 layout blocks each rendered frame): end drop 4 m, 173 frames, 0 inside, min clearance 0.20 m; ramp side drop, 132 frames, 0 inside, min clearance 0.20 m; the hard-landing runs also report 0 inside. Screenshots drop-end-0..2, drop-end-after, drop-side-0..2, drop-side-after. Limits: browser runs used camera yaw 0 and the three drag-rotated views, not every yaw.

assumptions: The Mixamo Hard Landing source has Hips rest rotation matching the avatar (both about identity), so the Hips rotation is applied as authored.
The 0.05 m ground tolerance is read per foot on the lowest of each foot's ankle and toe joints, because the ankle joint alone is 0.088 m above the sole even when standing flat.
Changing fall to a planted pelvis is acceptable scope because the no-pop and within-0.05 requirement at touchdown cannot hold with feet hovering 0.4 m up; I flagged it for QA.
decisionsProposed: Ship Hips height only where a clip needs it (land, fall) via HIPS_MOTION_CLIPS in config.ts. Keep every other clip and the hero idle Hips-free.
Camera obstacle query: Rapier ball cast with stopAtPenetration false, pull in at once, ease out with restoreK.
landing fade (ANIMATION.fade.land) lengthened from 0.1 to 0.15 s so the fall to land impact has no step above 0.07 m per frame.
lessonsProposed: When a retargeted clip's Hips are stripped, any crouch or bent-leg pose floats the feet. Derive a vertical Hips height from foot joints on the avatar skeleton and test the lowest foot per frame on the real bone tree.
Measure each foot separately: the lowest-foot metric hid a trailing foot raised 0.13 m.
Linear crossfade between a crouch and standing dips the feet under both poses (about 7 to 10 cm). Use a one-sided Hips lift after the mixer update.
Use gltf-transform nodes by unique name: a duplicate node name made GLTFLoader rename a track to Hips_1 and the track silently did not bind.
A camera that lags a falling pivot ends inside slabs; sphere-cast it, and test it with real physics against every collider each frame plus a no-query red case.
